item.title: Titans vs. Cowboys live updates, inactives, where to watch: Christian Parker hands off play-calling as 4-6 Cowboys chase NFC East lead
item.description: The Cowboys defense will look to bounce back after a historically bad start under first-year DC Christian Parker.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday's matchup between the Tennessee Titans and the Dallas Cowboys looks poised for high-scoring madness, as the two worst defenses in the league face off.

Dallas and Tennessee are one-two in total offensive yards allowed this season, with both defenses boasting more than 3,900 yards allowed by opponents. But while the Cowboys' offense has been able to salvage a 4-6 record, the Titans are 1-8, with just a surprisingly good offensive line holding the team together.

Dallas tried to reset the issue by stripping first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties, and having senior defensive assistant and veteran coach Mike Pettine call the plays going forward.

Tennessee, meanwhile, appears to be actively tanking. But the team did opt to keep star running back Tony Pollard, who should provide some offensive entertainment against a Cowboys defense that, in the words of their own head coach, "tackled like s***" last week.

In the AFC, the Buffalo Bills (8-1) can maintain the NFL's best record with a win over the Miami Dolphins (1-8). Meanwhile, the Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) hope to break free from a four-team logjam in the conference by beating the Arizona Cardinals (3-7). The Denver Broncos will need a win to stay with the Chiefs. They'll face a Las Vegas Raiders team (4-6) that hopes to have Brock Bowers in the lineup during the late afternoon schedule. The star tight end is battling an ankle injury.

Closing out Sunday's slate, the San Francisco 49ers (8-1) seek to maintain the NFL's best record as they face the Minnesota Vikings (7-2) in Mexico City. Receiver Mike Evans is listed as questionable but is expected to play.

item.title: Micah Parsons to practice in pads on Sunday
item.description: The Packers plan to have defensive end Micah Parsons on the field against the Rams on Wednesday night and Parsons will check off one more box toward that return to action at practice on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers plan to have defensive end Micah Parsons on the field against the Rams on Wednesday night and Parsons will check off one more box toward that return to action at practice on Sunday.

Head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters at a press conference that Parsons will practice in pads for the first time since he got back on the practice field earlier this month. LaFleur called it "the next marker" for Parsons to clear before he gets the green light to face the Rams.

LaFleur said the team will have a plan in place for how many snaps Parsons would play in his first game since tearing his ACL last December.

“He is an elite player, he's an elite athlete. I do think you see with many of these guys — I never want to put limitations on anybody, but he hasn’t played football in a long time. You gotta be conscious of that."

The Packers will release their first injury report for Week 12 later on Sunday and injury designations for the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game will be released on Tuesday.

item.title: Former ESPN analyst and NFL linebacker Tom Jackson dies at 75 years old
item.description: Jackson worked at ESPN for nearly 30 years after retiring from the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Longtime ESPN analyst and former NFL linebacker Tom Jackson has died. He was 75.

Jackson was a fixture on ESPN's NFL coverage after his playing career ended in 1986. He joined the network in 1987 and worked alongside Chris Berman for nearly 30 years until his retirement in 2016.

"Tom was a Hall of Famer in every sense of the word."

Our friend Tom Jackson left a lasting impact on everyone around him ❤️ pic.twitter.com/GuwqkneMIJ

— SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 22, 2026

Berman eulogized his friend and colleague during ESPN's "Sunday NFL Countdown," expressing his shock after seeing Jackson weeks ago at the network's studios in Bristol, Connecticut, and talking to him last week.

“We’ve lost one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet.”

Chris Berman announces the death of his longtime broadcast partner and best friend, Tom Jackson.

What an iconic duo for all those years. Thank you, TJ ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0eogqMa73r

— NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 22, 2026

"All of us are stunned. We've lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet," Berman said. "I was fortunate, as you know, to work side-by-side with him for 30 years on 'NFL Primetime' and 'NFL Gameday,' now 'Sunday NFL Countdown.'"

"Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst," he added. "There was nobody kinder, there was nobody more thoughtful, more loyal, more engaging than Tom Jackson."

Jackson died on Friday, according to Berman. His family informed ESPN of his death soon thereafter.

The undefeated Colts went to Dallas today trying to improve to 10-0 on the season.

Tony Romo who was making his first career start at home had other plans as Dallas upset the Colts. Boom and TJ have the highlights here! pic.twitter.com/HT8UeEE0w9

— 20 Years Ago Sports (@20YearsAgoSport) November 19, 2026

Jackson is known to generations of NFL fans for his work providing commentary on highlights for ESPN with Berman, long before pro football studio shows like "NFL Live" and the NFL Network became ubiquitous.

Watching clips of the day's games was never more electric than when the two detailed the action on screen with ESPN's iconic background music playing behind them during "NFL Primetime."

One of Jackson's signature bits was showing the week's hardest hits on Monday night, saying players got "Jacked Up!" Though that segment was eventually phased out as concern and consideration for head trauma and serious injury grew, Jackson conveyed the excitement and thrill that so many fans felt while watching the NFL.

Before going into broadcasting, Jackson was a linebacker for the Denver Broncos for 14 seasons. He played on two Super Bowl teams in 1977 and 1986, and ranks fourth in team history with 191 games played.

The Denver Broncos are heartbroken by the passing of Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history. pic.twitter.com/MdcpkuyKYs

— Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 22, 2026

Denver's 1975 fourth-round pick out of Louisville, Jackson was named to three Pro Bowls and twice earned All-Pro honors. The Broncos inducted Jackson into their Ring of Fame in 1992.

We are deeply saddened by the passing of Hall of Fame broadcaster, former Denver Bronco and Cardinal Forever, Tom Jackson.

Our thoughts are with his family, friends, teammates and everyone who knew him. pic.twitter.com/Y4mODdtlcb

— Louisville Football (@LouisvilleFB) November 22, 2026

At Louisville, Jackson played for fellow former ESPN analyst Lee Corso from 1970-72. The Cardinals also paid tribute to Jackson, who led the team in tackles in each of his three seasons. He was named the Missouri Valley Conference player of the year twice during his college career. Louisville honored his jersey No. 50 in 1999.

NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said Jackson “brought credibility, passion and humor to everything he did.”

“The NFL lost a wonderful man with the passing of Tom Jackson,” Goodell said in a statement. “Along with millions of fans, I will always remember him as a player and broadcaster, but also as a friend. He was an outstanding player whose toughness and leadership helped define an era of Broncos football. He brought credibility, passion and humor to everything he did, and generations of fans came to know him through his work at ESPN. Tom helped fans enjoy and better understand football, always bringing the perspective of someone who loved the game and the people who play it. More importantly, he earned the respect and friendship of players, coaches and everyone who had the privilege of knowing and working with him.”

item.title: Remembering Denver Broncos legend Tom Jackson
item.description: Tom Jackson, 1951-2026. Gone, but forever remembered.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos Country woke to the news of the legendary Tom Jackson’s passing. He was 75.

For those of us old enough, he is remembered as one of the stalwart members of the Orange Crush defense of the late 70s. He played for the Denver Broncos from 1973 to 1986.

The issued the following statement this morning:

“The Denver Broncos are heartbroken by the passing of Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history.

“An inspirational leader and fierce competitor, TJ was a proud member of the Broncos’ first Super Bowl team that helped establish a winning tradition in Denver. Off the field, Tom carried himself with class, warmth and humility, forging deep connections and lifelong friendships with teammates and throughout Broncos Country.

“TJ’s dynamic personality, quick wit and football knowledge made him a natural for television and paved the way for a Hall of Fame broadcasting career. For generations of fans, Tom was an iconic fixture on ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown and NFL Primetime, sharing his thoughtful insight with an unmistakable sense of humor that defined an era of sports broadcasting.

“Above all, TJ loved the Broncos and was a cherished member of our family for more than 50 years. We extend our deepest sympathies to Tom’s wife, Jennifer, his daughters, Taylor and Morgan, and all of his family, friends and teammates.”

He played in 191 career games, which still ranks fourth in team history. He was a two-time All-Pro and a three-time Pro Bowler. He finished his career with 1,531 total tackles, 44 sacks, 20 interceptions, eight fumble recoveries, and three touchdowns. He was a sole addition to the Broncos’ Ring of Fame in 1992 — his first year of eligibility for the honor.

For those not quite old enough for the playing days, Tom Jackson had a second career that may have been more impactful on the youth in America. In 1987, he teamed up with Chris Berman on Sunday NFL Countdown and NFL Primetime that went on to win seven Sports Emmy awards over the decades.

As kids, many of us would find the only way to catch the weekend’s action was through their highlight show. Many a fond childhood memory exists there, I am sure.

The team has announced they will be holding a pregame moment of silence and a video tribute to honor Tom Jackson before today’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Quite the fitting moment for a man who once taunted John Madden after a 30-7 beatdown in Oakland in 1977 by yelling, “It’s all over fat man!” from across the field.

Tom Jackson, 1951-2026. Gone, but forever remembered.

item.title: Steelers vs. Eagles: Week 11 game picks
item.description: Steelers vs. Eagles game picks.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and Philadelphia Eagles will face off on Sunday at 1:00 EST. The Steelers are hoping to avoid losing consecutive games for the first time this season, while the Eagles are looking to end a seven-game losing streak. Who will come out on top? Our staff weighs in.

Ryland Bickley: I’ve bet against history once this year, unwisely picking the Steelers to beat the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football in Week 4. And you know what? I haven’t learned my lesson. Yes, the Steelers haven’t won in Philadelphia since the ’60s, but this Eagles team is a mess.  After floundering against Joe Burrow and the Bengals last week, the Steelers defense should be able to find its footing against Joe Milton and a struggling Philly O-line. On the other side of the ball, I’m not too confident in Aaron Rodgers and co. to get things going on the road, but getting Roman Wilson back certainly helps. I think Pittsburgh does just enough to rebound from last week and win an ugly game on the road. Steelers 20, Eagles 17.

Mike Nicastro: Mike Nicaatro: The Steelers haven’t won in Philadelphia since 1965, but they’ll enter their house of horrors against a much different Eagles team. The Eagles have a depleted offensive line, an underwhelming run game, and they are on their third quarterback in Joe Milton. Unfortunately for the Steelers, their offense also leaves much to be desired. Father time might have officially hit Aaron Rodgers at the worst time, and DK Metcalf can’t seem to catch a cold in the winter. However, the black and gold are getting healthier at wideout, as Michael Pittman and Roman Wilson appear to be on track to get a helmet. That will help mitigate the challenges, and in an absolute rock fight, the Steelers offense will make a few more plays than the Eagles. Steelers 16, Eagles 10.  

Austin Bechtold: Lyndon B. Johnson was president, the Steelers played in Oakland at Pitt Stadium, and the Penguins weren’t even a team yet. These are all true events from the last time the Steelers beat the Eagles in Philadelphia in 1965. This game SHOULD be a different story. The Steelers need a significant bounce-back week after being embarrassed in primetime against the Cincinnati Bengals. They only had 40 yards of total offense at halftime and the defense couldn’t slow down a red hot Bengals offense. This is a turning point in the season and will go one of two ways: the Steelers dominate Philadelphia and attempt to show the Bengals game was a fluke, the Steelers and Eagles play a close game down to the end and whoever has the ball last will walk away with a victory. Joe Milton starts for the Eagles and the team hasn’t scored more than 21 points since Week 2 against the Titans. The Steelers get Roman Wilson back and should help the passing game, but losing Mason McCormick is likely a big loss up front. The Eagles are also getting healthier off their bye week. I don’t feel great about this game, but I think the Steelers will do enough for an ugly win. It would be great to see them force three turnovers and put together over 350 yards of offense to get back into form. The Steelers win for the first time in 61 years, but it’s not pretty! Steelers 20, Eagles 13.

Joey Bray: Joey Bray: We are all exhausted by the insult stat reminding us the Steelers haven’t won a game in Philadelphia since 1965. Still, this might be the Steelers’ best shot at winning in Philly in years. The Eagles are losers of seven straight, and for good reason. Their season has been defined by injuries and controversy. With Joe Milton starting at quarterback, his inexperience makes the chances of him being able to pick apart the Steelers’ lackluster secondary quite low. The Steelers offense looks to be getting some receiver help back, but how much will that actually help what has been a bad passing attack over the course of the last month? With Mason McCormick out indefinitely, I’m interested to see how the run game fares with Spencer Anderson back in the starting lineup. Ultimately, the Steelers pass rush needs a huge bounce back game. While the Steelers should still be able to rely on their run game against and Eagles defensive line that ranks 25th in the league. I’ll take the Steelers to get back on track and break the Philly curse in a close one. Steelers 23, Eagles 20.

Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers are the better team facing a third-string quarterback. The Eagles’ defense has also struggled this season, currently sitting at 27th in EPA per play. However, they still have several players on that side of the ball capable of slowing down a Steelers offense that doesn’t have a passing attack. The Steelers win, but it’s low-scoring and closer than anyone would like it to be. Steelers 17, Steelers 13.

Let us know what you think in the comments. Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more!

item.title: Jets fans are split on whether Geno Smith or Cade Klubnik should start at quarterback
item.description: In Week 10, Cade Klubnik got his first NFL regular season action in relief of an injured Smith. Klubnik played most of the Jets’ second half loss to the Buffalo Bills. In Week 11, it appears Smith will regain his starting role. We asked fans in our SB Nation Reacts survey whether this is the […]
item.content:encoded:
In Week 10, Cade Klubnik got his first NFL regular season action in relief of an injured Smith. Klubnik played most of the Jets’ second half loss to the Buffalo Bills.

In Week 11, it appears Smith will regain his starting role. We asked fans in our SB Nation Reacts survey whether this is the right call. A narrow majority said Klubnik should start this game.

That is about as close of a result as you can get.

It should be noted, however, that we asked a similar question a week ago, and only 28 percent of Jets fans voted that Klubnik should start.

It seems like merely seeing Klubnik on the field was enough to sway a large number of fans because his play against Buffalo certainly wasn’t spectacular.

Overall Jets fan confidence is down after the loss to the Bills. Only 20 percent of voters say they are confident in the team’s direction down from 28 percent last week.

I’m not sure much a win over the Chargers will improve confidence, but I could see the number falling into single digits with a loss along with the proportion of fans who want to see Klubnik rising quite a bit.

item.title: Chiefs-Cardinals Inactives: DT Peter Woods to miss third straight game
item.description: Kansas City and Arizona have released their inactive player lists for Sunday’s game.
item.content:encoded:
The Kansas City Chiefs have released their list of inactive players for Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals.

Running back Kenneth Walker, tackle Jaylon Moore, guard Trey Smith defensive tackles Peter Woods and Omarr Norman-Lott and cornerback Melvin Smith will not dress. Rookie Garrett Nussmeir has been designated as the third quarterback and is eligible to enter the game should starter Patrick Mahomes and backup Justin Fields become unavailable.

Walker (groin), Smith (concussion) and Moore (ankle) had already been ruled out on Friday’s final injury report. Woods (neck) and Norman-Lott (knee) had been deemed questionable, but the team will hold them out at least one more week. Norman-Lott is a listed inactive for the first time this season as the Chiefs added him to the active roster on Wednesday with his practice window to return from the Reserve/Physically-Unable-to-Perform list expiring. Norman-Lott has spent the first half of the season continuing to recover from an ACL tear suffered in 2025.

Woods left Week 9’s contest against the Denver Broncos with a neck injury. The first round rookie will now miss his third straight game.

With a short turnaround before Thursday’s road game against the Buffalo Bills, the Chiefs were expected to be conservative with injuries against the Cardinals.

On Saturday, Kansas City elevated running back Nate Carter and center Pete Nygra from the practice squad. As elevated players, they will automatically be returned to the team’s practice squad after the game. Carter and Nygra are both active for the contest.

The Cardinals have also released their list of inactives.

Quarterback Carson Beck, cornerback Starling Thomas V, offensive linemen Kingsley Eguakun and John Gaines II, and former Chiefs practice squad defensive tackle Andrew Billings will not go for the Cardinals.

Obviously, the biggest name on Arizona’s list is Beck. The team turned to the rookie quarterback after former Chiefs backup Gardner Minshew suffered a season ending elbow injury in Week 9. However, Beck was a midweek downgrade in practice with back spasms. Despite being ruled questionable to close the week, Arizona downgraded Beck to outon Saturday before leaving for Kansas City.

40-year-old journeyman backup Josh Johnson — who has been with the team less than two weeks — will start for the Cardinals. Johnson has not appeared in game in 2026.

Gaines had already been ruled out with an ankle injury.

The Cardinals elevated practice squad wide receiver Zay Jones for the matchup. Jones is active for the game.

item.title: Chris Berman honors 'best friend' Tom Jackson in emotional farewell
item.description: The football world paid tribute to Tom Jackson after his death. His longtime ESPN partner, Chris Berman, had tears in his eyes as he shared the news.
item.content:encoded:
Tom Jackson, who was a stalwart of ESPN's NFL coverage alongside Chris Berman, has died at the age of 75. The longtime analyst and Denver Broncos legend received an outpouring of support from all corners for the sports world for his contributions to the game on and off the field.

No tribute was more poignant than Berman's.

Berman, the long-time co-anchor alongside Jackson on "NFL Countdown" and "NFL Primetime," announced Jackson's death on Sunday morning.

“We’ve lost one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet.”

Chris Berman announces the death of his longtime broadcast partner and best friend, Tom Jackson.

What an iconic duo for all those years. Thank you, TJ ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0eogqMa73r

— NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 22, 2026

Chris Berman statement on Tom Jackson's death

In addition to his on-air tribute, Berman released a statement further detailing his admiration for Jackson and his former partner's impact both personally and professionally:

All of us are stunned. I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL PrimeTime and Sunday NFL Countdown. It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.

Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst. There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom’s was frequent and unmistakable. He is easily summed up by this classic old song – “He’s got sunshine on a cloudy day.”

Nobody knew this better than his wife Jen and his daughters Taylor and Morgan. Our hearts bleed for them. We thank them for lending Tom to us.

Tom was my best friend professionally and personally. If you ever met him or just knew him from watching ESPN, he was your best friend too.

Jackson joined ESPN in 1987 where he was partnered with Berman, with "Sunday NFL Countdown" winning Sports Emmy awards for Outstanding Studio Show seven times.

Jackson was inducted into the Denver Broncos Ring of Fame in 1992.

Tom Jackson tributes pour in

Berman wasn't the only one to honor Jackson. Others from around the sports world paid tribute to the NFL titan on Sunday:

The Denver Broncos are heartbroken by the passing of Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history. pic.twitter.com/MdcpkuyKYs

— Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 22, 2026

Orange ties for the entire @ESPNNFL Sunday NFL Countdown crew. 🧡

TJ will forever be part of the Broncos and @espn families. pic.twitter.com/Z0SG8bTNFE

— Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 22, 2026

We are deeply saddened by the passing of Hall of Fame broadcaster, former Denver Bronco and Cardinal Forever, Tom Jackson.

Our thoughts are with his family, friends, teammates and everyone who knew him. pic.twitter.com/Y4mODdtlcb

— Louisville Football (@LouisvilleFB) November 22, 2026

RIP Tom Jackson: you are an icon and one of the very best ever - on and off the field. 🙏🙏 pic.twitter.com/B7PWtdmR2S

— Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 22, 2026

Before there was Red Zone, the Sunday Ticket, back in the days of NFL blackout rules…watching NFL Primetime was the way you saw what happened in most NFL games…
So we all spent countless Sunday evenings with Tom Jackson and Chris Berman…feels like we all lost a friend..RIP https://t.co/sxavXAp1ll

— Bob Wischusen (@espnbob) November 22, 2026

Just speaking for myself, but I truly believe “NFL PrimeTime” with Chris Berman and Tom Jackson was the most important studio show of my lifetime.

— Jimmy Traina (@JimmyTraina) November 22, 2026

Before the Internet, before RedZone … there was a Sunday evening ritual called NFL Primetime.

TJ and Boom, just two pals talking football. What a time 🫶 pic.twitter.com/Da1RVuCCOL

— ESPN (@espn) November 22, 2026

item.title: Chris Berman announces Tom Jackson’s death in emotional tribute on ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’
item.description: Chris Berman grew emotional Sunday while discussing Tom Jackson, his longtime ESPN broadcast partner, who died Friday at 75.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Berman grew emotional Sunday while discussing Tom Jackson, his longtime ESPN broadcast partner, who died Friday at 75.

“He was a vital 75,” Berman said on ESPN’s “Sunday NFL Countdown” show. “Tom was poignant. He was active. This is a shock.”

Berman, who said he spoke “at length” to Jackson as recently as Tuesday, also called the former Broncos linebacker “one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet.”

He quoted The Temptations hit song “My Girl,” saying Jackson always “brought sunshine on a cloudy day.”

“All of us are stunned,” Berman read from a statement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown.

“It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.”

ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro added that Jackson — a three-time Pro Bowler over 14 NFL seasons with the Broncos — was “one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN’s history.”

“He brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans,” Pitaro said. “Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends. In fact, ESPN’s NFL studio is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio, a distinction unmatched in our history and a fitting tribute to their lasting impact.

“Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure.”

Jackson retired from ESPN in 2016 but returned for a digital edition of “NFL Primetime” alongside Berman in 2019.

He had been awarded the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television award by the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015, an honor which Berman also had earned in 2010.

Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and two daughters, Taylor and Morgan.

item.title: Fantasy Football: Jaylen Waddle finally shows up, Bears' backfield goes off and more bold predictions for Week 11
item.description: Our Yahoo analysts share their one bold call for fantasy football in Week 11.
item.content:encoded:
There aren't many weeks left in the fantasy football regular season; you can't hold anything back. That means you need to be bold to come out on top. Our Yahoo analysts share their one bold prediction for fantasy football in Week 11.

Jaylen Waddle turns in second WR1 finish of '26

I realize that trusting any WR tied to Bo Nix is like playing with fire. But there have been some fantasy-related improvements to Denver's passing game. First, Nix is throwing more relative to expectations. He's been at a +3.0% PROE over the last month, a 180-degree flip from Weeks 1-4 (-2.5%). He's also throwing to the middle of the field, where passing efficiency jumps, at the sixth-highest rate. And he's fifth in EPA per dropback on those throws.

That's where Jaylen Waddle comes into play. He's led the Broncos in targets on concepts over the MoF (2.49 YPRR). That's where the Raiders have been consistently beaten on defense. Opposing WRs are averaging 87.6 YPG and a smooth 24.8 PPR PPG on those throws alone. While both were on broken plays, both Seahawks' WRs found themselves in the end zone with the ball on throws between the numbers. Assuming Waddle clears protocol, he'll give us his second WR1 performance of the season in Week 11. — Chris Allen

Swift, Monangai both finish as top-12 fantasy RBs

The Bears' backfield will finally be at full strength in Week 11 with Kyle Monangai returning after a five-game absence due to a toe injury. He's picked the right defense to get back on the field against, since the Saints are allowing the second-most fantasy points to RBs, the eighth-most rushing yards and the fourth-most rushing touchdowns. Chicago also has an implied total of 30 points, so we can project a lot of scoring from Ben Johnson's crew.

New Orleans has let 11 different backs reach double-digit fantasy points, including three sets of teammates. One of those duos was Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr., who both finished as top-12 fantasy RBs in Week 4. Monangai and D'Andre Swift also accomplished that feat in the opener versus the Panthers, which was one of the four games they've shared the field together this season. Get ready for them to do it again, now that the bar is lower with six teams on bye. — Justin Boone

Chig Okonkwo finishes as a top-5 fantasy TE

Over the last month, Chig Okonkwo has the seventh-best TE volume and a top-5 route share when accounting for his Week 10 injury. He still has the big-play ability he's had throughout his career and can turn his volume into better production against a Bengals defense ranking bottom-5 versus TEs. Cincinnati is forcing opposing offenses into going pass-heavy, is able to slow down receivers on the outside, but has still allowed the second-most yards on the fourth-most targets to TEs inside, without playing against any of the top fantasy tight ends. If Okonkwo has the ball in his hands that much, he's bound to make some big plays after the catch. — Joel Smyth

Cam Ward finishes as a top-10 fantasy QB against Dallas

I know Cam Ward's name hasn't exactly been synonymous with fantasy scoring, but he's quietly put together two pretty damn good games. Dallas, meanwhile, has been loudly awful on defense for more than two seasons. New defensive play-caller this week? Cool. I'm still calling a top-10 finish for Ward. He's thrown for 535 yards and four touchdowns over his last two games and added another 80 yards on the ground. Dallas is giving up 7.8 yards per pass attempt and has already allowed 19 passing touchdowns. Brock Purdy just hung 389 yards and three scores on them in 28 attempts. Ward doesn't have to do all that. Give me 250 through the air, two touchdown passes and another 35 on the ground. And if Dak Prescott gets Dallas out to an early lead, good. That's more chances for Ward to throw against a defense I'm still going out of my way to attack. — Ray Garvin

Tony Pollard has six catches or 80 yards receiving (or both)

The Titans normally don't throw the ball much to Pollard, but that's changed in the last three games — the underrated back has collected 14 catches in that span. And the Dallas defense is especially terrible when it comes to tracking running backs in the passing game — Christian McCaffrey had a field day against this unit last week. Tennessee's offense has been up to code in the last three weeks, and this game features a 54.5-point total. Pollard is going to crush in his revenge game against the Cowboys, and part of the story will be written through the air. — Scott Pianowski

Christian McCaffrey catches double-digit passes

On the surface, maybe this doesn't sound bold but funny enough, McCaffrey has done this just once in over 60 regular and postseason games with the 49ers. It happened last season when he caught 10 passes against the Cardinals in a low-scoring game. The 49ers lead the league in getting five players out in the route, accounting for 75% of their dropbacks. That's unlikely to change against Minnesota and its blitz looks. I expect McCaffrey to be heavily involved as a receiver in the flats, as an escort screen option and on extended checkdowns. There will be voids in coverage against Minnesota there and Brock Purdy has been excellent at picking the right spots to attack. — Matt Harmon

Emeka Egbuka is a top-15 WR

Egbuka has been more good than great on tape this year. He battled a toe injury in training camp and then has picked up new injuries along the way. Baker Mayfield said he "looks great right now" after hinting that the injuries have prevented him from taking off earlier this year. For what it's worth, Egbuka is not on the injury report at all right now and that was not the case earlier this year.

Across the entire season, Egbuka is the WR33 on WR19 usage. Those are probably closer to his floor. We'll see if the Bucs going to more Tez Johnson forced Eguka to play outside more, but to put things simply, the Buccaneers are desperate for Egbuka to turn into an alpha. Everyone else doesn't have the skills to do that, and the pass game has been unwatchable. I can argue he is still frequently the designed first read on a bulk of the Bucs' dropbacks. Everyone has to just play better.

The Lions are too injured at all three levels to be nervous about the matchup. The Bucs are unlikely to be in full run the clock out mode like they've been in the past, and it doesn’t sound like CB1 D.J. Reed (hip) will suit up. — Hayden Winks

item.title: Drake Maye’s reported recovery timeline leaves door open for potential return
item.description: The Patriots quarterback is dealing with a fractured fibula.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots will be without their starting quarterback for most of the remaining regular season, but there is a chance he does eventually come back in 2026.

Drake Maye, who exited last Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions with what was initially announced as an ankle injury, will miss “at least six weeks” due to what was since diagnosed as a broken fibula. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network was first to report the recovery timeline.

“He is out at least six weeks with a fractured fibula,” Rapoport said on the air on Sunday. “Six weeks from now is January 3rd. So, there’s an outside chance if the Patriots make the playoffs with Tommy DeVito as their starting quarterback, that potentially Drake Maye could come back.”

If the timeline presented by Rapoport holds, Maye might be back in time for a Week 17 game against the Denver Broncos or the regular season finale versus the Miami Dolphins a week later. The first round of the NFL playoffs will start on January 15.

Maye suffered the injury on the very first drive of the Patriots’ 35-10 loss to the Lions, quickly getting ruled out for the remainder of the contest. The nature of the ailment prevented the 24-year-old from flying back from Germany to the United States with his teammates; instead, he underwent further treatment in Munich before being ready for the transatlantic journey.

The Patriots have not made any official announcements yet about Maye, and he does remain on their 53-man roster as of Sunday. However, considering the severity of his injury and the team’s current quarterback depth chart, the belief is that backup Tommy DeVito will continue leading New England’s offense for the foreseeable future.

DeVito’s first game as the Patriots’ starter will come next Sunday against the Chargers.

item.title: New York Jets vs Los Angeles Chargers Pre-Game Ball
item.description: Garrett Wilson is primed for a big game against the Chargers
item.content:encoded:
Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit.

One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. 

This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it.

Today, for the first time in three weeks, we’re not handing out a pre-blame ball. The Jets have a plausible path to victory against the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers, so pre-game ball it is. The pre-game ball for the Jets game against the Chargers goes to (drum roll please) – Garrett Wilson!

The Chargers have a pretty good run defense. They allowed just 15 rushing yards last week against the Baltimore Ravens. They have held five of nine opponents under 120 yards rushing, and they have allowed just 3.9 rushing yards per attempt for the season. This could be a fairly difficult afternoon for the Jets’ running game.

The passing game is a different story. The Chargers rank 28th in the NFL in net yards allowed per passing attempt. The Chargers also struggle to get to the quarterback, with just 15 sacks for the season. The top receivers on opposing teams have routinely excelled against the Chargers’ mediocre secondary. The loss of Derwin James at safety has badly hurt the Chargers’ secondary, and their mediocre cornerbacks have not been able to compensate.

The Jets will be missing Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams against the Chargers, leaving Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as the primary targets for Geno Smith in the passing game. With Wilson in the midst of his best season in the NFL, Smith is likely to look his way early and often against the porous Chargers secondary. This feels like a setup for a monster game for Wilson.

Garrett Wilson, come on down! You’ve earned today’s pre-game ball for the Jets. Let’s see you torch the Chargers’ secondary on the way to a Jets victory today.

What about you? Who would you give the pre-game or pre-blame ball to? Let us know in the comments.

item.title: How long is Jalen Hurts out? Injury update as Eagles QB recovers from blood clots
item.description: When will Jalen Hurts return? The Eagles are still missing their quarterback as he deals with blood clots.
item.content:encoded:
For a fifth straight game, the Philadelphia Eagles will be without their usual leader on offense.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts remains out in Week 11 as he continues to deal with the blood clots diagnosis he received in October. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported at the time of Hurts' diagnosis that he is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season.

Since Hurts landed on injured reserve on Oct. 17, the Eagles have had two quarterbacks start games. Joe Milton III will make his second career start – and second in a row – against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

NFLPA INQUIRY: NFL, Roger Goodell 'welcome' investigation into Jalen Hurts' blood clot care

Philadelphia is on a seven-game losing streak coming out of their bye in Week 11. Hurts had led the Eagles to three straight losses before his injury, and the team's fill-in starters have gone 0-4 in the time since.

Here's everything to know about Hurts' blood clot situation:

Jalen Hurts injury update

Hurts is out again in Week 11 as he continues to undergo treatment for his deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli diagnosis. The primary treatment for the blood clotting issue is using anticoagulants – blood thinners – the use of which prohibits participation in contact sports.

The Eagles' quarterback is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season as he recovers from the blood clots, according to multiple reports.

What happened to Jalen Hurts?

Hurts was diagnosed with a deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli ahead of the Eagles' Week 6 game, according to a joint statement from his agent – Nicole Lynn – and the Eagles. In simpler terms, Hurts is dealing with blood clots in both of his lungs.

Hurts was initially diagnosed with superficial vein thrombosis while in London for Philadelphia's Week 5 clash with the Jaguars. A superficial blood clot, according to medical experts, is not as severe a risk as deep vein thrombosis, but they still need to be taken seriously.

Ultimately, the Eagles determined at the time that Hurts was clear to play in the game on Oct. 11. NFL Media insider Ian Rapoport reported that Hurts played in Week 5 after staying in the hospital until 4 a.m. the night before. The quarterback played through the game and flew back to the United States from London with the rest of the team.

One week later, Hurts underwent more imaging and discovered that his superficial clot had become a more serious case of deep vein thrombosis. In addition, blood clots had moved to his lungs – a situation that could have turned lethal without treatment.

The treatment for Hurts' condition will consist of using blood thinners, which will disqualify him from participating in contact activities for a while. He'll miss several months – and potentially the remainder of the 2026 season – as he treats the blood clots.

JALEN HURTS: What happened to Eagles QB? Blood clots explained

Will Jalen Hurts ever play football again?

Hurts' future in football is up to him, but all indications are that he will return at some point.

"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery," Lynn, Hurts' agent, wrote in her joint statement with the Eagles. "We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects."

The statement points to Hurts' eventual return to football. Barring a shocking announcement, the Eagles' quarterback will likely return either late this year or at the start of the 2027 season.

Eagles QB depth chart

With Hurts out for an extended period of time, here's how Philadelphia's quarterbacks room stacks up in Week 11:

  • Joe Milton III
  • Tanner McKee
  • Cole Payton

Milton is on his third team since the Patriots drafted him in the sixth round in 2024. New England traded him to the Dallas Cowboys last April, and the Eagles signed Milton off of the Cowboys' practice squad on Friday, Oct. 16, after Hurts' injury. He took over McKee's job as fill-in starter in Week 9 and is set to make his second career start in Week 11.

McKee has been with the Eagles since they drafted him in the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He went 0-3 as a starter this year before losing the job to Milton. Payton is a fifth-round rookie out of North Dakota State and was a two-time FCS national champion with the Bison.

item.title: Lions LB Jack Campbell sent 'thrilled' coach a gameday text: Latest injury update
item.description: Lions LB Jacks Campbell has been sidelined since a scary neck injury during Week 8, but he "really excited" his defensive coordinator with an update.
item.content:encoded:
Even when he's not around the team, Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has figured out how to get his teammates and coaches pumped up.

The Lions are back stateside after their trip to Munich but remain without Campbell for a third week after the linebacker suffered a neck injury during the Detroit's Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings. On Thursday, Nov. 19, Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said he received a text from the sidelined linebacker on game day last week that "fired me up."

"I miss the hell out of Jack, if I'm being honest," Sheppard said. "But his teammates have done a tremendous job making sure that he knows that we’re doing this clearly for him.

"Still sending thoughts and prayers out to Jack and his wife, Megan, his son and his family as he continues through his recovery process. I was excited to get a text from him for the first time on game day, so that kind of fired me up a bit there. I was very thrilled about that."

JACK CAMPBELL: Linebacker sent Detroit Lions DC a text that fired him up

Sheppard declined to share the content of the text but said it was the first time he had heard from Campbell since his injury.

"That really excited me, man," Sheppard said.

The Lions placed Campbell on injured reserve on Nov. 7. Updates have been few and far between, with the most notable news coming via a statement from Campbell on Nov. 4. In that update, the linebacker revealed he had movement in his lower body and was making progress with movement in his upper body.

Detroit was victorious in its first two game without Campbell, winning 19-9 over the Miami Dolphins in Week 9. In Week 10, the Lions dominated in front of the German crowd in Munich, downing the New England Patriots 35-10.

Here's what we know about Jack Campbell's injury as the Lions roll into a Week 11 clash with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

KELVIN SHEPPARD: Lions' DC says text from Jack Campbell 'fired me up'

Latest Jack Campbell injury update

Jack Campbell has been placed on injured reserve, the Lions announced on Nov. 7.

The linebacker announced in a statement on Nov. 4 that he had full movement in his lower body and was continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body. During a Fox broadcast of the Lions game against the New England Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 15, play-by-play announcer Joe Davis said Campbell is expected to make a "full recovery."

“I spoke to him before we left," Dan Campbell said after the Lions beat the Patriots. "He is good spirits, and he continues to get better every day. I did not get into details of this trip, I just wanted him to know ‘I’m still thinking about you, and just stay the course.’”

Is Jack Campbell still in the hospital?

Campbell remained hospitalized and was continuing to improve, according to CBS Sports' Melanie Collins on Nov. 8. Collins said on a pregame broadcast that Campbell said that while he doesn't want any tears or sympathy, he does want to get back on the field.

Campbell on Wednesday, Nov. 4, thanked his caregivers at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit and the Detroit Lions medical staff.

What is Jack Campbell's condition?

Campbell announced in a statement on Nov. 4 that he has full movement in his lower body. He is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body.

It was the first concrete update on Campbell's condition since the injury occurred on Sunday, Nov. 1. Prior to Campbell's statement, the team had issued more general updates, saying that preliminary results were positive.

REGGIE BROWN: Ex-Lions LB reflects on life-altering injury after Jack Campbell hospitalized

What happened to Jack Campbell?

Campbell went down with a neck injury after tackling Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson.

He stayed down as the training staff and medical personnel surrounded him and a cart arrived. Campbell was loaded onto a backboard before the cart took him off the field. He was transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury after exiting the team's Week 8 win over the Vikings.

Who is Jack Campbell?

Campbell is a linebacker for the Detroit Lions.

The 26-year-old is in his fourth NFL season, all with Detroit. The Lions drafted Campbell with the 18th overall pick in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft after he starred in college for the Iowa Hawkeyes.

A native of Cedar Falls, Iowa, Campbell broke out during his junior season with the Hawkeyes, totaling 143 tackles, two interceptions, two fumble recoveries and a sack in 2021. Returning for his senior season, Campbell was named an All-American in 2022 and received the Butkus Award as the top linebacker in college football.

He also received the William V. Campbell Trophy, also known as the "academic Heisman," in 2022 for being recognized as the college football player with the best combination of academics, leadership and on-field performance.

More: Jack Campbell is a Lions team captain. Here's why his teammates love him

Campbell slid right in as a key piece of the Lions' defense after arriving in the NFL. However, he didn't officially break out until his third season. Campbell recorded 176 total tackles, three forced fumbles and five sacks en route to being named a first-team All-Pro and earning his first Pro Bowl appearance last season.

On May 21, 2026, the Lions recognized Campbell's breakout with a four-year, $81 million extension.

item.title: New-look Cowboys defense must contain Tony Pollard
item.description: How will Tony Pollard do against the Cowboys?
item.content:encoded:
The 4-6 Dallas Cowboys meet the 1-8 Tennessee Titans this week at AT&T Stadium. Here are three keys to the game.

Tony Pollard is the threat

If Dallas removes Titans running back Tony Pollard from the equation, this offense doesn’t have a ton on firepower elsewhere. The Cowboys currently possess the NFL’s worst running defense while Pollard has gone over 100 yards twice out of the last three weeks. This run defense needs to buckle down this week.

The former Dallas running back has the speed to make a defense pay when reaching the second level. He’s also a major receiving threat, catching eight balls for 66 yards last week against the Jaguars. The Cowboys defensive front cannot allow the speedy back to operate in space, whether it’s in the box or on the perimeter.

With Cam Ward throwing for over 200 yards just three times this season, the strategy is simple for the Cowboys. Remove the threat in the backfield and the Titans offense should struggle to move the ball. Allow Pollard to cook and it could be another long day.

Expose a weak Titans secondary

The Titans secondary is extremely vulnerable. They rank dead last in pass defense, allowing the most passing yards through ten weeks. Injuries haven’t helped the already struggling back end of that defense.

After a three touchdown day against the 49ers from George Pickens and an excellent season from CeeDee Lamb, this should be a game that showcases plenty of silver and blue fireworks. Coach Brian Schottenheimer needs to remain balanced but will find plenty of space for the Cowboys receivers to operate throughout the day. It’ll be important to adjust the script to attack that lackluster Titans secondary while also remaining somewhat committed to keeping Javonte Williams busy on the ground.

Protect Dak and finish drives

If there is one thing that could disrupt the Cowboys offense against the Titans, it’ll be the injury to Tyler Booker and a pass rush that can get hot. Tennessee edge Jacob Martin has 7.5 sacks on the season, tying him for seventh place alongside T.J. Watt and David Bailey.

The aforementioned balanced offensive attack will be important in keeping the Titans defense guessing. There will be shots for the Cowboys offense to take through the air. But with the injury to Tyler Booker, establishing the run with backup guard T.J. Bass should be one of the key focal points. Nothing settles offensive lineman quite like the ability to consistently move forward.

If the Cowboys can block up front and keep Dak Prescott clean, Dallas possesses plenty of ability to finish drives with touchdowns. This could indeed be another huge week for these receivers.

The New York Jets activated veteran wide receiver Sterling Shepard from the practice squad ahead of their game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is out for today’s game with an ankle injury, leaving the Jets short at wide receiver.

Sterling Shepard is a 33 year old, 5’ 10”, 195 pound wide receiver. He was originally drafted out of Oklahoma by the New York Giants with the 40th overall pick in the 2nd round of the 2016 NFL draft. Shepard was an effective receiver for the Giants early in his career. He spent the first eight years of his career with the Giants before moving on after the 2023 season. Shepard played with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024 and 2025 before being signed as an unrestricted free agent by the Jets in 2026. Unfortunately, Shepard likely has little left to offer the Jets. He will turn 34 years old in February. Shepard has not exceeded 400 receiving yards in a season, a 50% success rate, or 7 yards per target since all the way back in 2020. The Jets might be better off giving practice squad receiver Jamaal Pritchett a shot. Pritchett has excelled each of the last two training camps, only to be buried on the practice squad in the regular season.

Regardless of whether the Jets elevated Shepard or Pritchett, they will be thin at wide receiver until Cooper makes it back. In the meantime, who knows, maybe Shepard has a turn back the clock performance left in his tank.

item.title: Broncos, TV legend Tom Jackson dies at 75
item.description: Tom Jackson, a 14-year veteran with the Broncos and a longtime fixture on ESPN's NFL programming, has died.
item.content:encoded:
Tom Jackson, a 14-year veteran with the Broncos and a longtime fixture on ESPN's NFL programming, has died. He was 75.

Jackson was a fourth-round pick of the Broncos in 1973. He became a full-time starter in his second season. He started a run of three straight Pro Bowl berths in 1977, the same year the Broncos made their first Super Bowl appearance.

Jackson played until 1986. The next year, he debuted on ESPN. He worked on the network's Sunday NFL Countdown show and the must-see NFL Primetime, which featured extended highlights packages years before the best plays could be instantly seen on social media.

"All of us are stunned," Jackson's long-time on-air partner, Chris Berman, said in a statement. "I'm stunned, we're stunned and you're stunned. We've lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown. It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week."

Jackson is a member of the Broncos' Ring of Fame, the franchise's 50th anniversary team, and the Louisville Ring of Honor. He received the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award from the Hall of Fame in 2015.

The recent changes to the Pro Football Hall of Fame's rules could make Jackson a candidate for the expanded "contributor" category, given that it allows former players to enhance their standing with other contributions to the game. Few have combined an impactful and prolonged playing career with an impactful and prolonged broadcasting career.

We extend our condolences to Jackson's friends, family, teammates, and colleagues.

item.title: Tom Jackson, ex-ESPN analyst and Denver Broncos great, dead at 75
item.description: Tom Jackson, a titan of ESPN's NFL coverage for nearly three decades and Denver Bronco icon, has died.
item.content:encoded:
Football heaven is now a little more “jacked up!”

Former NFL All-Pro linebacker and ESPN studio analyst Tom Jackson died, his family told ESPN. He was 75.

Jackson was part of the Denver Broncos’ "Orange Crush" defensive units from 1973 to 1986. Upon his retirement, he immediately joined ESPN and was Chris Berman’s partner on the desk for shows such as "Sunday NFL Countdown" and "NFL Primetime."

Berman announced Jackson died Friday, Nov. 19, unexpectedly. No cause of death was provided.

"He was a vital 75 … this is a shock," said Berman, who hosted Jackson – one of his best friends – in the studio for a visit recently.

"We’ve lost one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet," Berman added.

On "Monday Night Countdown," Jackson executed one of the most anticipated segments in sports television for a time – “Jacked Up!” showed the hardest hits in football from that week. He and Berman became a quintessential pairing that brought excitement to highlights that may have already been watched before but felt like they were being viewed for the first time.

To honor Jackson, the entire "Countdown" crew sported orange ties Sunday. ESPN’s NFL studio is named after Jackson and Berman.

“Tom Jackson was one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN’s history,” ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said.

Tom Jackson football career

Jackson was inducted into the Broncos’ Ring of Fame in 1992 and ranks third on the team’s all-time games played list. He published an autobiography in 1987, “Blitz: An Autobiography.”

“He was an outstanding player whose toughness and leadership helped define an era of Broncos football,” NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. “He brought credibility, passion and humor to everything he did, and generations of fans came to know him through his work at ESPN.

“More importantly, he earned the respect and friendship of players, coaches and everyone who had the privilege of working with him.”

A son of Ohio, Jackson grew up in Cleveland and died in Cincinnati. He played collegiately at Louisville and was drafted by the Broncos in the fourth round (88th overall) in the 1973 draft. He was "a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history," the Broncos said in a statement.

We are deeply saddened by the passing of Hall of Fame broadcaster, former Denver Bronco and Cardinal Forever, Tom Jackson.

Our thoughts are with his family, friends, teammates and everyone who knew him. pic.twitter.com/Y4mODdtlcb

— Louisville Football (@LouisvilleFB) November 22, 2026

"An inspirational leader and fierce competitor, 'TJ' was a proud member of the Broncos' first Super Bowl team that helped establish a winning tradition in Denver," the statement read. "Off the field, Tom carried himself with class, warmth and humility, forging deep connections and lifelong friendships with teammates and throughout Broncos Country."

Jackson earned the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award from the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015 and retired the next year.

"Having joined in the early stages of ESPN and remained with the same company for 29 years is especially gratifying," Jackson said at the time. "This move just comes at a time when the priority of my life is spending time with my family."

As a player, Jackson helped the Broncos reach two AFC title games and was a first-team All-Pro in 1977.

Jackson is survived by his wife Jen and his two daughters, Taylor and Morgan.

"If you ever met Tom, or just knew him from watching our shows on ESPN, he was your best friend, too," Berman said.

item.title: Week 11 NFL odds, picks, predictions: Our best bets for this week's games
item.description: Our NFL handicappers give out their favorite bets for Week 11 games.
item.content:encoded:
Week 11 of the NFL season began with the Houston Texans taking care of business and easily defeating the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on Thursday night.

What will the rest of the weekend have in store for bettors?

Our NFL handicapping team of Matt Jacob, Jeremy Pond and Matt Russell combine to give their best bets for Week 11 of the NFL season.

Odds subject to change.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-6.5, 45.5)

Jacob: How flawless was Lions quarterback Jared Goff through the first six games of the 2026 season?

He put the ball in the air 223 times and not once did it land in the hands of the wrong team. In the past three games, though, Goff has gotten quite charitable. He threw one interception against Minnesota in Week 8, one against Miami in Week 9 and two against New England a week ago in Germany. In all, four INTs in his last 81 pass attempts.

The good news for Goff: He hasn't been picked off in four straight games in more than four seasons (Weeks 3-7 in 2022). The bad news: This week, the 2016 No. 1 overall pick is facing a Tampa Bay defense that has recorded an NFL-high 16 INTs.

In their most recent game — a 27-24 Week 9 loss at Chicago — the Bucs picked off Caleb Williams four times. They did the same thing the previous week to Atlanta's Michael Penix Jr. And in the five games prior, Tampa intercepted every QB it faced at least once.

In fact, the Buccaneers' defense has nabbed at least one interception in eight of nine games. And oddsmakers are offering plus money that they won't do the same thing against a suddenly turnover-prone Goff? Take it.

Bet: Jared Goff over 1.5 interceptions (+121)

Pond: Despite the fact Baker Mayfield (foot sprain) returned to practice in a limited capacity Thursday, he will be far from 100 percent if he takes the field against the Lions.

Without a mobile Mayfield, I would imagine head coach Todd Bowles will resort to his two-headed, top-ranked ground attack featuring Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell. The Buccaneers took this approach two weeks back when the pair combined for a jaw-dropping 52 carries and 310 yards on the ground in a 16-0 rain-soaked win against Atlanta.

With that likely game plan, Tampa Bay will do all it can to control the clock and keep Goff and the Detroit offense off the field. And that means we could see a low-scoring affair at Ford Field.

Six of the Buccaneers' past eight games have seen a combined total of 45 points or less, so I'm taking a shot that their methodical offense and top-ranked defense can keep this one close.

Bet: Under 46.5 points alt total (-115, FanDuel)

New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5, 49.5)

Russell: In the NFL, absence makes the heart grow fonder, or, in the case of the Bears, it makes the betting market forget about four interceptions by Caleb Williams, and a non-spread-covering win over the Buccaneers. At least that's what this point spread indicates, as it's five points clear of the Bears last-known betting line,  against Tampa Bay. 

The Bears, with added pieces to their defense and a thrill-a-minute offense, are the darlings of the NFC at the moment. The type of thing that happens when you win three straight games, all in primetime. The result? A rating in the betting market that makes Chicago the perceived best team in the NFL. 

There are four other double-digit point spreads in Week 11. Three of them involve rookie quarterbacks, and the fourth was Daniel Jones and the Colts at Houston. This is not that. 

Coming into Thursday night, Jones was 29th out of 31 qualifying quarterbacks in adjusted EPA/Play, while Tyler Shough is slotted in the middle of the NFL pack. 

Unlike the Colts — or the Cardinals, Dolphins and Raiders — the Saints are actually getting healthier as the season goes on, with the return of left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr., first-round pick Jordan Tyson and No. 1 tailback Travis Etienne in the past two weeks. Needing overtime to beat Shedeur Sanders and the Browns at home and a loss to the Panthers (on a last-second 54-yard field goal), hasn't helped market perception of New Orleans, but judging the Saints off the entire season has made them underrated.

Especially since a somewhat healthy version won at Baltimore and almost did so at Detroit in their first two games, showing what they're capable of at full strength.

Bet: Saints +11.5

Jacksonville Jaguars (-5.5, 46.5) at New York Giants

Jacob: New York's offense has been far more productive this season than expected — particularly considering the team's merry-go-round at quarterback. While cycling through Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy, the Giants have put up at least 19 points in seven of nine games.

The exceptions: a 28-6 Week 2 loss at the Rams (the game where Dart suffered his season-ending knee injury) and a 12-7 Week 3 win over the Titans. Overall, New York has topped 20 points seven times and tallied at least 27 five times.

Now for the "but": Of the eight teams the Giants have played, only one currently ranks in the top 18 in scoring defense. That team? The Rams (who, to repeat, held New York to two field goals). Including two games against Washington, the Giants' opponents enter this week with the following scoring-defense rankings: fifth (Rams), 18th, 19th, 20th, 26th, 28th, 30th and 31st.

New York's Week 11 foe? It fields the NFL's second-stingiest defense. Not only does Jacksonville yield just 16 points per game, but only five opponents have eclipsed 10 points; only three have cleared 17; and only two have topped 20 (Houston put up 34 in London in Week 6, and Tennessee scored 23 last week).

The only other team to exceed 20 points against Jacksonville in the last 17 games — 15 of which the Jags have won? Arizona (24 points in an overtime loss in Week 12 last season).

McCarthy and the Giants are unlikely to join that list Sunday, especially in what are expected to be soggy conditions at MetLife Stadium.

Bet: Giants under 20.5 total points (-130)

Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3.5, 46.5)

Pond: You couldn't ask for a better Sunday night clash than this showdown between NFC powerhouses in Mexico City. And it will pit San Francisco's explosive offense against Minnesota's stingy defense, which concedes just 14 PPG.

The 49ers have been the poster child for first-half dominance, not trailing once at the break and boasting an 8-0-1 record through 30 minutes of play. MVP candidate Brock Purdy and RB Christian McCaffrey have this San Francisco offense clicking right out of the gate, which I expect to be the case again.

Meanwhile, the Vikings look like a completely different team with the return of Kirk Cousins under center. As my colleague Ben Fawkes reported, Minnesota has been popular in Super Bowl futures wagering after its 30-10 dismantling of Green Bay last week at Lambeau Field.

As for the total, we're going to see some tired legs late in this game due to the unforgiving altitude (7,352 feet above sea level) in Mexico City.

Combining the thin-air angle and Minnesota having the league's best defense leads me to believe Kevin O'Connell's outfit will have a big second-half advantage, putting it in position to win this game outright.

Expect a tale of two halves in a close game where points will be at a premium.

Bets: 49ers 1H ML (-115) | Vikings +3.5 (-118) | Under 47.5 (-130) at FanDuel

item.title: Tom Jackson, former Broncos star and ESPN legend, dead at 75
item.description: The Hall of Fame broadcaster’s family informed ESPN of his death.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos legend and former ESPN voice, Tom Jackson, died on Friday at 75, Adam Schefter reported Sunday morning.

The Hall of Fame broadcaster’s family informed ESPN of his death and no cause has been revealed.

He is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and his two daughters, Taylor and Morgan.

Jackson, a fourth-round pick by the Broncos in the 1973 draft out of Louisville, became a fixture of the Denver defense. However, his post-NFL career as a broadcaster is how most know him.

The three-time Pro Bowler went on a 29-year run with the Worldwide Leader and was a staple alongside Chris Berman, who announced his death during “Sunday NFL Countdown.”

“All of us are stunned,” Berman said in a statement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown. It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.”

He concluded his NFL career in 1986 and played in 191 regular-season games and 10 playoff matchups with the Broncos across 14 seasons.

The Broncos will hold a pregame moment of silence and a tribute video to honor Jackson against the Raiders on Sunday evening, the organization’s chief communications officer shared.

“The Denver Broncos are heartbroken by the passing of Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history,” the organization wrote in a statement Sunday. “An inspirational leader and fierce competitor, TJ was a proud member of the Broncos’ first Super Bowl team that helped establish a winning tradition in Denver. Off the field, Tom carried himself with class, warmth and humility, forging deep connections and lifelong friendships with teammates and throughout Broncos country.

“TJ’s dynamic personality, quick wit and football knowledge made him a natural for television and paved the way for a Hall of Fame broadcasting career. For generations of fans, Tom was an iconic fixture on ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown and NFL Primetime, sharing his thoughtful insight with an unmistakable sense of humor that defined an era of sports broadcasting.

“Above all, TJ loved the Broncos and was a cherished member of our family for more than 50 years. We extend our deepest sympathies to Tom’s wife, Jennifer, his daughters, Taylor and Morgan, and all of his family, friends and teammates.”

Jackson’s final assignment with ESPN was the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s enshrinement ceremony in 2016. Yet, he returned for a digital-only edition of “NFL Primetime” in 2019 and reunited with Berman.

He was awarded the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television award by the Hall of Fame in 2015, which came five years after Berman took home the same honor.

item.description: The Badgers had a big day offensively in Week 12.
item.content:encoded:
The Wisconsin Badgers blew out the Purdue Boilermakers 42-10 on Saturday afternoon, securing a key win as they improved to 7-4 on the season and 5-3 in conference play with one game to go.

Wisconsin’s offense set the tone early with touchdowns on each of its first three drives, and Purdue could never catch up in the blowout.

Here are the PFF grades and snap counts on offense for the Badgers against Purdue in Week 12.

Quarterbacks

Colton Joseph – Snap Count: [62], Grade: 83.7

Deuce Adams – Snap Count: [10], Grade: 43.0

Colton Joseph led the entire offense with an 83.7 PFF grade in one of his best days of the season. Joseph had 187 rushing yards and two touchdowns on the ground, as we saw what the offense could look like with Joseph’s rushing threat being fully utilized.

Wisconsin didn’t have to rely on Joseph as a passer much, with the quarterback throwing for 114 yards and 6.3 yards per attempt. But his ability as a runner broke this one open and led the Badgers to the win.

Wisconsin committed to Darrion Dupree as its lead back, and he went for 125 yards and two touchdowns on 7.8 yards per attempt. It was Dupree’s best game by a wide margin this season, marking the first time he topped 65 yards, and nearly matched his career high of 131 rushing yards set in the Illinois game last year.

Bryan Jackson still got 10 carries, while Abu Sama remained phased out of the game plan. It looks like Wisconsin will lean on Dupree and Jackson the rest of the way.

But Jaylon Domingeaux led the team with three catches for 39 yards, while Jacob Harris had three catches for 32 yards. In the passing game, it was a ton of quick concepts, as Jeff Grimes looked to get the ball out of Colton Joseph’s hands.
